cells.tense: Present — here, with the pen, letting it go as you see it.
cells.verb: letting what can't hold fall away
cells.place: in the choosing of where you're headed
cells.ask: Give the direction that survived a small steady hour each day — nothing showy, just kept lit — so that the next time something falls, it's because you saw through it, not because you got restless.
cells.core: You're letting the wrong things fall, and it isn't an accident. When something you were aiming at turns out to be built on nothing, you see it, you set it down, and what's left standing is what was actually true. That kind of clearing doesn't leave a mess behind it. It leaves room — and room is the one thing a direction needs to become a practice.
cells.sheetLine: What falls is only what needed to. What stands is yours to work.

cells.tense: Future — bracing toward a cleared field that keeps not arriving.
cells.verb: knocking things down before they've shown whether they hold
cells.place: in the choosing of where you're headed
cells.ask: Find one thing that people before you have carried a long way and learn why it lasted before you decide about it — let one old way stand long enough to be understood, and what falls after that will be what truly couldn't hold.
cells.core: You're tearing things down faster than you can tell whether they were holding. Somewhere ahead is a place with nothing false left in it, and you're trying to get there by demolition, so every direction you pick gets dismantled before it can take you anywhere. It feels like freedom while you're doing it. Afterward it's mostly rubble, and no road through it.
cells.sheetLine: You're calling it freedom. Nothing's been allowed to stand.

cells.tense: Past — still propping a door that's already behind you.
cells.verb: holding up what has already stopped holding
cells.place: in the choosing of where you're headed
cells.ask: Don't force the letting go. Build one small thing that actually works now — a shape for this week, a plan you can look at and have it make sense — and the propped-up thing will come down on its own once something real is standing next to it; what falls then will be what needed to.
cells.core: You're holding up something that already stopped holding you. The direction you're pointed in quit making sense a while back, and you've been standing in that doorway since, keeping it propped — not because it leads anywhere, but because letting it fall would mean choosing again. Your arm is tired. The door is still open. It's just behind you now.
cells.sheetLine: You're keeping up a direction that already let you down.

cells.tense: Disowned present — pen down, in a room that's already shifting.
cells.verb: not seeing what's about to give way
cells.place: in the choosing of where you're headed
cells.ask: Before anything falls, go back to the plainer question: where do you actually want to go today, in your gut? Follow that honest pull for one afternoon and notice what it won't fit through — that's the thing that's going, and seeing it first is what turns a collapse into a clearing.
cells.core: Something you're aiming at is about to give, and you don't see it yet. You're steering by a structure that stopped being true, and the strain is showing up around you — in what keeps not working, in choices that feel oddly heavy — but ask you and the direction is fine. The giving-way is already underway. You're just not the one watching it.
cells.sheetLine: Something's coming down. You haven't looked yet.
